title: Consolidate usage-event ingestion and schema validation into a resilient service
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Console emits usage events from frontend and backend agents. Current ingestion paths are distributed across two services (ingest-proxy and schema-gatekeeper) which causes duplication, schema drift, and difficulty coordinating rollouts. Goal: Build a consolidated ingestion-validator service that centralizes ingestion, performs streaming schema validation, enriches events with tenant metadata, and writes to the analytics topic with clear failure semantics and observability. Constraints: Zero data loss for production events, preserve existing event contracts for hosted customers, low-latency (<150ms P95 for API path), and ability to opt into strict validation per customer. Non-goals: Re-implement full replay/backfill tooling in this ticket; change public SDK event shapes except for optional metadata fields. Success metrics: Reduce schema rejection noise by 90% through better validation errors and guidance, reduce end-to-end ingestion latency P95 by 30% in canary, and eliminate duplicate schema checks in downstream consumers.
acceptance_criteria: New service accepts existing event formats without schema changes when strict mode is off
Validation errors are emitted to a dead-letter topic with enriched error context
Canary deployment in us-west2 handles 10% of traffic with no customer-facing errors
Dashboards show per-schema validation rate, rejection reasons, and per-tenant error counts
End-to-end tests that simulate malformed, partial, and larger payloads are added and pass in CI
tasks: Design API surface and compatibility layer for existing ingest clients
Implement streaming validator using existing JSON Schema ruleset and add custom hooks for Redwood-specific types
Add tenant enrichment by calling tenant metadata service with caching layer
Write to primary analytics topic and dead-letter topic with headers indicating validation status
Add feature flag to enable strict validation per tenant
Create end-to-end integration tests and local simulator for load testing
Instrument tracing and metrics (latency histogram, validation rejection counter, DLQ bytes)
Run canary with 10% traffic and monitor for 72 hours before ramping
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Strict validation may surface large numbers of malformed events from old SDKs leading to backlog. Mitigation: Start with strict=false for all tenants, enable DLQ and per-tenant opt-in via feature flag. Provide automatic mapping rules to repair common issues (timestamp formats, missing optional fields). Add back-pressure circuit breaker for tenant spikes and consumer lag monitoring.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy service behind traffic-split with 0% traffic; 2) Run schema-only mode to shadow validation for 48 hours; 3) Canary with 10% traffic strict=false for 72 hours; 4) Enable strict validation for internal tenants and monitor; 5) Gradually enable strict for more tenants guided by DLQ metrics and PM outreach
testing_strategy: Unit tests for validation hooks, contract tests against known event fixtures, integration tests with Kafka test cluster, chaos test injecting malformed events, load test simulating 5k rps to validate latency and memory behavior
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-schema rate, rejection reasons, DLQ depth, write latency. Alerts: DLQ depth > 1GB sustained, validation rejection rate > 1% for 1 hour, P95 ingestion latency > 150ms. Pager policy: on-call backend team primary, product analytics secondary
